841-statistics: The Program Adviser may approve substitutes. Arts and Science students: see Science's Course Overlap rules.
842-general-scientific-principles: A second field course from the program may count. One of BREE 529, ENVB 529 or GEOG 314; one of GEOG 322 or BREE 217; one of ANSC 326 or BIOL 324.
843-program-description: How food and infectious agents connect health to the environment, and how farming, insecticides, climate, deforestation, urbanization and dams shift those links. Good interventions depend on knowing how people respond to them.
Cellular looks at the physiological level; Population looks at the ecosystem level: society, land and population health. Cellular is for B.Sc.(Ag.Env.Sc.) and B.Sc. Environment Majors only.
844-cellular-biology: LSCI 202 and 211 and BIOL 200 and 201 overlap: holding both of one pair blocks credit for either of the other.
844-hormones: No ANSC 424 after both PHGY 209 and 210. No PHGY 210 after both ANSC 323 and 424.
844-physiology: No ANSC 323 after both PHGY 209 and 210. No PHGY 209 after both ANSC 323 and 424.
845-ecology: Only one each of ENVR 540 or BIOL 540, BIOL 451 or NRSC 451.
847-advanced-ecology: Only one each of ENVR 540 or BIOL 540, BIOL 451 or NRSC 451.
847-list-a: 6 credits, at most 3 from any one category.
847-decision-making-techniques-and-manag: An advanced quantitative methods course can count with Adviser approval. Only one each of AGEC 200 or ECON 208, ENVB 529 or GEOG 201.
848-list-b: 9 credits, at most 3 from any one category.
848-program-description: 63 credits with the core, for B.Sc.(Ag.Env.Sc.) and B.Sc. Environment Majors only. Statistics for environmental science: you learn to design studies and analyze environmental data. Mostly statistics and applied math, plus ecology, soils, water and impact assessment so you can talk with specialists. Two complementary axes, and an internship.
848-suggested-first-year-u1-courses: See the Bieler School's Student Handbook. Check prerequisites and equivalents with your adviser: you get no credit and no warning for a course equivalent to one you already took.
BIOL 373 or AEMA 310 are possible in U1, but skip them if you plan Option 1, since they overlap MATH 324.
849-statistics: 6 credits from one of two options. Many statistics courses overlap, especially MATH 324. See Science's Course Overlap rules; they don't apply to B.Sc.(Ag.Env.Sc.) students.
850-list-1: At least 3 credits, or equivalents of BREE 252 or BREE 319.
850-program-description: 63 credits with the core, for B.Sc.(Ag.Env.Sc.) and B.Sc. Environment Majors only. More people need more food, from better yields or new land, but farming can harm biodiversity and waterways, and it competes with cities, transport, water, timber and biofuels. Shrinking land makes informed decisions matter more.
850-program-prerequisites-or-corequisite: Required: a biology and a chemistry course, or CEGEP equivalents such as objectives 00XU and 00XV.
851-domain-complementary-courses-36-cred: 18 of Fundamentals, 12 of Applied Sciences, 6 of Social Sciences or Humanities. Choose from one subtopic or several.
851-fundamentals-18-credits: One statistics course or equivalent, plus one from each of five pairs. Science's Course Overlap rules apply.
852-natural-resources-and-natural-resour: Only one each of BIOL 465 or WILD 421, BREE 217 or GEOG 322.
852-environment-management: One of BREE 529, ENVB 529 or GEOG 201.
853-program-description: 63 credits with the core, for B.Sc.(Ag.Env.Sc.) and B.Sc. Environment Majors only. Thin soil layers control water, nutrients and energy for ecosystems and help produce greenhouse gases, and they are stressed by desertification, erosion, deforestation and climate change. Prepares you for graduate work in earth system science, hydrology or landscape ecology.
853-domain-complementary-courses-39-cred: 3 each of statistics, GIS, and weather and climate; 9 of land surface processes; 3 of environment and resource management; 3 of field course; 3 of social science; 12 of advanced studies from Lists A and B.
855-program-description: 63 credits with the core, for B.Sc.(Ag.Env.Sc.) and B.Sc. Environment Majors only. Sustaining what ecosystems give people, from food and clean water to beauty, with humans treated as part of the system.
You learn what drives natural populations, how to manage ecosystems for goals, the economic and social forces involved, long-term effects of management, and monitoring methods.
855-program-prerequisites-or-corequisite: Required: a biology and a chemistry course, or CEGEP equivalents such as objectives 00XU and 00XV.
857-program-description: How atmospheric and human processes shape water environments and how those link to ecosystems. Biological stream: life in water bodies. Physical stream: how water moves and changes, from rivers to oceans and air.
857-program-requirements: At most 30 credits at the 200 level, and at least 12 at 400+, counting required and complementary courses.
858-water-environments-and-habitats: Only one each of BIOL 540 or ENVR 540, ENVB 210 or GEOG 305.
859-surface-and-atmospheric-processes: Only one each of ATOC 219 or CHEM 219, ENVB 529 or GEOG 201, EPSC 522 or GEOG 522.
859-engineering-mathematics-hydrology: Only one each of ENVB 529 or GEOG 201, ENVB 530 or GEOG 506, ENVB 210 or GEOG 305, AEMA 305 or MATH 315, EPSC 522 or GEOG 522.
